items.name: action-menu
items.title: Action menu
items.description: A button with popovertarget and a popover list of real links and buttons: a click already opens, closes and activates items with no script. With JavaScript this adds the ARIA APG menu button keyboard model (roving tabindex, arrow keys, Home/End, typeahead) and a teental-staggered entrance. Quiet is a ruled list; warm is ink-ruled; playful is stamped.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today about 7.0 KB: behaviour (action-menu.js + action-menu.core.js) 6.7 KB; skins quiet, warm and playful are each a no-op mount (about 0.2 KB each), because the look is entirely in action-menu.css keyed off [data-skin]/[data-open].

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: A word or two of status. The text is the meaning, a distinct shape per tone backs it up, colour comes last. Quiet is text with a hairline rule; warm is a hand-inked outline in the tone's ink; playful is a chip of colour with a kolam flower on the corner. Busy badges breathe or turn, never in quiet or under reduced motion.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 11014 bytes: behaviour (badge.js + badge.core.js) 7.4 KB, skins quiet 0.2 KB, warm 2.1 KB, playful 1.3 KB.

items.name: booking
items.title: Booking
items.description: Book the whole house, or a room, in four steps built from every Wave 2 part: dates with the season ribbon, guests and room, your details with the phone confirmed by a code, and a signature to confirm and hold, with breakfast as a switch. A live quote from the booking kernels shows every band's nights, GST on its own line and the deposit, calls provisional figures provisional, and shows no figure for a single room the card does not price. The hold is stamped Held. A prototype that sends, holds and charges nothing, and says so; without JavaScript every step shows and the form validates and submits.

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: A native <button> or <a href>, unchanged, with the register's drawing laid over it: quiet is a hairline outline; warm is a hand-inked outline that boils gently on hover or focus; playful is a stamped chip that presses in and blooms an ink ring on release. Forced colours bring back the browser's own control.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today about 7.0 KB: behaviour (button.js + button.core.js) 4.4 KB, skins quiet 0.2 KB, warm 1.3 KB, playful 1.1 KB.

items.name: chat-thread
items.title: Chat thread
items.description: A conversation as a list of messages a screen reader can read, instead of a screenshot. Phone numbers, emails and names are taken out at build time and replaced by a marker that says what was removed. Quiet is a ruled transcript like a court record; warm puts each message in a hand-inked bubble on paper; playful uses bright bubbles that bounce in as they scroll into view. Replies quote the earlier message ("Replying to:" for screen readers) and reactions are read once, as words.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Element 4.1 KB, pure core 10.2 KB (redaction, markup with replies and reactions, the bubble), skins quiet 0.3 KB, warm 2.5 KB, playful 1.1 KB.

items.name: check
items.title: Checkbox
items.description: A native checkbox that submits, validates and takes Space with or without JavaScript. Quiet is a hairline box with a crisp tick drawn by CSS; warm sketches the box in four pencil strokes whose corners cross and draws a heavy tick in by hand; playful is a little rubber-stamp block, and stamps a bold tick over its edge, printed through the stamp's ink texture. Indeterminate, and a "select all" box that goes checked, mixed or clear with its children. Forced colours bring back the system checkbox.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 16519 bytes: behaviour (check.js + check.core.js) 9.5 KB, skins quiet 0.2 KB, warm 2.2 KB, playful 4.2 KB. The playful skin also imports inkMask from stamp.core.js.

items.name: combobox
items.title: Combobox
items.description: An input with suggestions. Without JavaScript it is the browser's own input list and datalist; with it, the ARIA APG editable combobox with a listbox popover, full keyboard support, and matching that finds places however people type them: without accents, by an older name, in another script, or spelled as heard. Warm writes it on the paper over the field's pencil rule, with a list ruled in pencil; playful is a stamped box with stamped chips.

budget.reason: Behaviour 13.2 KB (0009 allows up to 16 KB with a reason): the APG editable-combobox keyboard model plus matching that folds Latin accents without touching Indic vowel signs, aliases across scripts and loose romanisation. Skins share a 1.2 KB caret and add 0.3 KB (quiet), 1.5 KB (warm) and 0.7 KB (playful); warm draws with field/rule.js, counted in field. Raised from 17 KB to 20 KB for the warm pencil rule (S5), well inside decision 0005's 12 KB plus 8 KB a skin, with about 15% headroom.

items.name: connecting
items.title: Connecting (FireflySync)
items.description: A connection's state in words, read out as it changes. Quiet shows a static dot; warm and playful show fireflies that blink on their own while connecting and fall into step (Kuramoto coupling) only once connected. Offline, they dim.

budget.reason: The contract's 12 KB behaviour plus 8 KB per skin, declared as the sum used: behaviour (connecting.js and connecting.core.js) about 6.6 KB, the warm and playful skins about 5.7 KB each including the shared fireflies.js, quiet under 0.4 KB.

items.name: core
items.title: Core
items.description: The register (quiet, warm, playful) and its cascade, the scene contract as defineScene, and the sg-scene element that runs any scene with its still, scrim, calm rects, toggle and status text.
items.stabilityReason: The scene contract and <sg-scene> have run every scene in the registry since the soft launch, with no breaking change yet.

budget.reason: Decision 0021: the open keep-away list, the reading-place watcher and the movable hook (the movable behaviour itself is its own item).

items.name: core-component
items.title: Core: components
items.description: SgElement and defineComponent: the light-DOM base every sg-* component extends. It enhances a native child, follows the register, loads one skin per register lazily, batches updates, pauses off screen and survives moves.

items.name: core-movable
items.title: Core: movable words
items.description: <sg-scene movable>: a grip on the reading panel that moves the words by drag or by arrow keys, clamped inside the stage, on frosted glass in warm and playful. The scene makes room live. Off in quiet and when the words sit below the picture. The page remembers the place: sg-words-moved out, words-at in.

budget.reason: Decision 0021: the element side (grip, pointer capture, keys, status, glass) and its pure geometry (movable.core.js, tested in Node, counted apart per decision 0010).

items.name: core-orient
items.title: Core: words in the world
items.description: Words on a plane that turns a little toward the reader and settles. The register sets the model, not the colour: quiet leaves the words flat and still, warm allows 6 degrees of tilt with a 0.9 s settle, playful 16 degrees with 0.45 s, and a touch screen or Save-Data steps one register down. The turn is one composited transform on the layer, so the text stays real and the layout never moves; quat.core.js is the maths (unit quaternions, shortest-path slerp, a frame-rate-independent damp), orient.core.js is the policy (the readability cone the plane is projected back onto, the seeded sway, the polite status line), orient.js is the only part that touches the DOM. unproject() hands a rect measured through the turn back to the flat plane, so a scene can keep judging occlusion in the plane's own space.

budget.reason: The element side (decision 0009, 12 KB) and the two pure cores counted apart (decision 0010, 12 KB together), so 24576. Today 23.2 KB: orient.js 11.9 KB, quat.core.js 5.6 KB, orient.core.js 5.1 KB. The check (orient.check.mjs) and the demo are not counted, as with every other piece.

items.name: date-range
items.title: Date range
items.description: Arrival and departure over two native date inputs that submit without JavaScript. With it, a two-month calendar that knows taken nights and turnover mornings from the booking kernels, moves like the APG date grid, feeds the kernels' reasons into native validation, and in warm and playful inks your stay under a season ribbon.

budget.reason: Parts per decision 0010: element date-range.js 15,050 bytes (over 12 KB, under 16 KB: the APG keyboard grid, turnover rules, native validation, the season table, the rates setter and open-from run in every register); pure core date-range.core.js 9,949 bytes (under its own 12 KB); shared skin helper skins/drawing.js 13,604 bytes, counted as one skin, over the 8 KB skin allowance because it holds the ink loops, the season ribbon and its phone-width key; skin files quiet 199, warm 312 and playful 309 bytes.

items.name: depth-photo
items.title: Depth photo
items.description: : a photograph (or a drawing) with a depth map, seen through a camera. The inside is the picture and its alt is what a screen reader hears. Live (three.js): the focus racks by depth with a circle-of-confusion gather, the camera dollies with true parallax, and the water moves inside a mask. 2D (quiet, reduced motion, lite devices, no WebGL, three blocked): the same frame at rest, the focus still racking, nothing moving on its own. Implements the frame contract for exact-frame export.

budget.reason: Decisions 0009, 0010 and 0017; the step from 40 KB to 45 KB (46,080) was accepted by the Sutradhar on 26 Sep 2026 (story 1). Today 42.8 KB: element 14.9 KB (0009, up to 16 KB: two renderers, the governor, the slow-machine rescue, context-loss recovery, the frame contract), pure core 3.8 KB (0010), the three.js renderer 15.4 KB (a look shader and a two-layer stage shader: near and far layers, dropped stretched pixels and a small inpaint, which the share card's smeared plate rim asked for), the 2D renderer 6.5 KB, register skins 2.2 KB. The rack-focus and frame helpers it took from story 1 are copied into story-shims.js (1.6 KB). Needs npm three 0.186.1 (npmDependencies) for the live tier only.

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description: A modal on the native <dialog>: showModal() traps focus and blocks the page, Escape closes it, focus returns to the opener. Any element with data-sg-dialog opens it; without JavaScript that element is a real link to a real page. Quiet is a plain dimmed backdrop; warm and playful are full-bleed with the Carepa surface behind a floating card, mounted only while open.

budget.reason: 0010: element (dialog.js) + core (dialog.core.js) together, since the pure core here is small (openersFor, isDismiss, STRINGS) and not worth a separate 12 KB allowance. Today 5781 bytes for behaviour, plus three skins (quiet 0.3 KB, warm 0.8 KB, playful 1.2 KB); Carepa itself is a separate registry item.

items.name: drawer
items.title: Drawer
items.description: A panel sliding in from an edge (start, end, top or bottom), on the same native <dialog> contract as Dialog: showModal() traps focus, Escape closes, focus returns to the opener. Quiet is a hairline panel; warm is a paper panel with a deckled edge over the Carepa surface; playful is the same, brighter, with the slide timed to the Teental cycle's first beat.

budget.reason: 0010: element + core together (5255 bytes today), plus three skins (quiet 0.2 KB, warm 0.7 KB, playful 1.1 KB, which also imports the shared talaDelay from packages/tokens). Carepa and the tokens' Teental export are separate registry items.

items.name: empty
items.title: Empty state
items.description: What a place shows before there is anything in it: your heading, sentence and action, named as a region. Quiet adds a hairline drawing; warm sets a scene (Paus, rain on a Goan window) beside the words, drifting slowly; playful lets you play with it. The scene loads only when a warm or playful page needs it.

budget.reason: Behaviour about 5.3 KB (empty.js 2.2 KB, empty.core.js 3.1 KB); skins about 0.9 KB (quiet), 2.4 KB (warm: the scene loads only once the empty state is on screen, and sits after the words in the document) and 0.3 KB (playful, which reuses warm). Declared with about 10% headroom. The scene it shows is its own registry item with its own budget.

items.name: engine
items.title: Engine
items.description: The pencil box every scene draws with: seeded randomness and noise, geometry, fields, ink and paper, the stage and loop, the quality governor, the sun and what it casts, things that lag and ring, fronts that cross a field, and a small WebGL helper.

budget.reason: Raised from 53,248 for light.js, motion.js and wave.js. All three are opt-in by import, so a scene pays only for what it names: mithagar draws on rng, math and color, 4,483 B of it. This figure is the whole pencil box, not a per-scene cost.

items.name: enquiry
items.title: Ask the house (enquiry)
items.description: The Casa Exemplo enquiry form rebuilt from library parts: a native form the browser validates, ruled fields that ink as you type, notes in the house's own words, a still line drawing of the house's front elevation in warm and playful, and a send that says plainly it is a prototype and sends nothing. Without JavaScript it validates natively and posts to a page that keeps nothing.

items.name: event-card
items.title: Event card
items.description: One workshop, class, supper club or pop-up: the kind, the title, the date and time, the venue, what you'll do and eat, the price per person and a booking link. It reads the clock in the venue's own time zone and says whether the event is coming up, today, on now or over; a seats line shows only when seats-left is given, sold out only when it is 0, and a finished event stops offering its booking link and says why. Quiet is a ruled card; warm is a ticket with a stub on a perforated line; playful is the same ticket, and the stub tears away a little when you point at it.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins; the pure core is budgeted apart (0010). Today 21,972 bytes: element 7.5 KB, pure core 11.3 KB (zones, the clock, the words, the calendar, the perforation), skins quiet 0.1 KB, warm 2.7 KB, playful 0.3 KB (it reuses warm's ticket).

items.name: event-list
items.title: Event list
items.description: A calendar of event cards that keeps itself honest: what is coming up is on top, soonest first; what has happened is put away in a closed "Before" drawer (a native details element); and when nothing is coming it says so in words, with your call to action beside it. When the clock passes an event while the page is open the card moves by itself, from a single timer that runs only while the list is on screen. Quiet is a plain ruled list; warm draws the empty state as a ticket with nothing printed on it yet; playful lets the hand show.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 8,415 bytes: element 6.8 KB, pure core 1.1 KB (it leans on event-card's core for the clock), skins 0.5 KB in all.

items.name: export
items.title: Export
items.description: A scene (or any canvas) to PNG, WebM and animated GIF. PNG uses canvas.toBlob; WebM records one requested frame at a time from canvas.captureStream(0), so a seeded run is reproducible however busy the machine is; GIF uses a small, dependency-free encoder (median-cut palette, an LZW core), tested against a reference decoder in Node.

budget.reason: Not a component (no registers, no skins): the whole package's behaviour, at roughly the component figure (0009) since export code runs the same way, a little over it once the real GCE/LZW fix and the pacing fix (webm.js) landed. index.js 0.5 KB, png.js 2.1 KB, webm.js 5.3 KB, gif.js 3.5 KB (the browser edges) plus gif.core.js 8.4 KB (the tested palette/LZW core, its own concern, like a component's *.core.js under 0010): 19.8 KB measured, budgeted with a little headroom.

items.name: field
items.title: Field (TextField, TextArea)
items.description: A label over a ruled line, for a line of text or a longer message, wrapping a native input or textarea that types, autofills, validates and submits without JavaScript. Quiet is the hairline rule under a writing well; warm writes on the paper itself, over a seeded pencil rule that inks from left to right on focus and under your words as you type, with a laterite exercise-book margin down a textarea; playful draws the same in accent ink with a thicker nib and wobbles on twos while you type. Counts characters near a maxlength, aloud only at 20, 10 and 0.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 21005 bytes: behaviour (field.js + field.core.js, and rule.js, the pencil rule select and combobox share) 12.4 KB, skins quiet 0.2 KB, warm 6.7 KB, playful 1.2 KB.

items.name: field-note
items.title: Field note
items.description: The note under a form field that says what is wrong and how to fix it. Follows constraint validation with its own wording (or shows a server message), never nags on the first try, wires aria-describedby and aria-invalid, focuses the first problem on submit. Quiet is small danger text with a mark; warm a margin note in the hand with a pencil arrow; playful inks it on and underlines it.

budget.reason: Decision 0009: 15 KB of behaviour (words in the person's terms, dates the way people say them, and a note that never appears mid-click and never repeats itself), plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 21939 bytes: behaviour (field-note.js + field-note.core.js) 14.3 KB, skins quiet 0.5 KB, warm 4.3 KB, playful 2.3 KB.

items.name: file-drop
items.title: File drop
items.description: A native file input you can also drop files onto. Without JavaScript it is the browser's own input; with it, the real input covers a drop zone, and the element checks accept, size and count, lists each file with a Remove button, and says every change in words. Quiet is a ruled zone; warm posts a letter into a pillar box; playful drops it in with a thunk.

budget.reason: Behaviour about 10.2 KB (file-drop.js 6.1 KB, file-drop.core.js 4.1 KB); skins 0.2 KB (quiet), 4.5 KB of post box shared by warm and playful (skins/post.js), 0.3 KB each for warm and playful.

items.name: file-upload
items.title: File upload
items.description: Choose photos and PDFs and watch each one arrive. Files too large are refused in plain words beside the field, a dropped file keeps its bar where it stopped and offers Try again, and a Received stamp lands once every file is safe. Each bar reads 99% until the server confirms, so the warm kolam closes only when the file has really arrived. Driven by a pure, seeded fake transport you swap for your own.

items.name: folio
items.title: Folio
items.description: The document layer's pieces that travel with a document: Markdown with directives (scene, diagram, price-table, timeline, signature, note), rendered to HTML by a pure parser with line-numbered errors; the print sheet and the script that makes scenes print their still; the seal (the policy, the hash and verify) and the in-page check that lets a reader hash their own copy. The builder that inlines, subsets, seals and prints (build/, bin/) is a Node dev tool with npm dependencies (esbuild, subset-font, Playwright), so it stays in the repo and is not copied.

budget.reason: Decision 0010 in spirit: the Markdown parser and directive renderer (md/index.js 22.9 KB, which checks a diagram's lines with folio-diagram's grammar,, md/parse.js 14.7 KB) are a pure core that runs in Node at build time and is fully tested; they never ship inside a sealed document. What a document carries is folio-print.js and folio-check.js, 1.9 KB together, and build/seal.mjs (3.6 KB) runs only in Node for folio verify. Declared at 44 KB: today 42.4 KB.

items.name: folio-diagram
items.title: Diagram
items.description: A diagram from a few lines of text (Guest -> Portal: books): boxes, arrows, flows with things moving along them, groups, and step-through. Drawn at build time as a static SVG with its text alternative from the same source, so it reads and prints without JavaScript. Loops back go round the side that meets no other box, each label sits beside its own line, and where one cannot, every connection carries its step number instead. <sg-diagram> adds the draw-in, the moving flows, step-through by buttons and keys, register changes, and turns a wide diagram downward on a narrow screen before its words would shrink below about 12 px. Quiet is a plain pen; warm and playful ink it by hand.

budget.reason: Decisions 0009 and 0010, with the core over its allowance. The element (diagram.js 12.3 KB) is within 12 KB to 16 KB. The pure core is diagram.grammar.js (5.0 KB: the line grammar, which Folio's Markdown also uses to check a diagram unbuilt) and diagram.core.js (20.7 KB: layered layout, loop routing, label placement and the text alternative), 25.6 KB together, over 0010's 12 KB because the layout is the diagram; it runs in Node at build time and is tested. render.js (7.7 KB) writes the SVG as a string, pure, and diagram.ink.js (3.5 KB) is the hand-inked line, one skin helper. Declared at 50 KB: today about 49 KB. A document built from Markdown carries all of them, since the element redraws in the page.

items.name: food-order
items.title: Food order
items.description: A menu and the way to order from it, for a small food business that takes orders on WhatsApp: a short note on how ordering works, a menu with a stepper on every dish you can order, and a composer that writes the order as a plain message (day with notice, time of day, delivery or pickup, area, name, notes), shows the exact words, and opens WhatsApp with them already in the box. With no JavaScript the menu is a readable list and the page keeps one plain wa.me link. It never says an order is placed: the person sends the message and the shop confirms.

items.name: form
items.title: Form
items.description: A native form the browser validates, which says what happens when you send it. Adds a field note to every field, summarises problems and focuses the first, and follows an sg-submit promise (or posts itself with fetch): Sending only while work is pending, then Sent or why it could not send, in one polite voice. Quiet is words only; warm and playful draw a Loader and a Stamp, and a failure is also a Toast. Without JavaScript it validates and submits natively.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 13510 bytes: behaviour (form.js + form.core.js) 10.8 KB, skins quiet 0.3 KB, warm 1.9 KB, playful 0.3 KB.

items.name: kantar-curtain
items.title: The tiatr curtain
items.description: The tiatr's red velvet curtain, drawn once: a tiled velvet strip with a slow sideways drift, a soft shadow under the pelmet, a gold fringe along a hem whose shape the caller supplies. The Kantar scene and the Kantar interlude both draw it from here, so there is one curtain in the library, not two. curtainEdge is pure and tested in Node; drawCurtain is the canvas side. It draws no text.

budget.reason: One small drawing module shared by the Kantar scene and the Kantar interlude; the velvet strip, the pelmet shadow and the fringe, with the hem supplied by the caller.

items.name: kantar-interlude
items.title: The Kantar interlude
items.description: A curtain between two steps of a long flow: it drops (with folds and a hem that ripples with a damped wave when it lands), a line plays in a warm spotlight pool while the real work happens (however long that actually takes, with a standing silhouette in playful), and it rises on the next step. Always has a skip control; never outlasts the real work unless the author raises minWaitMs on purpose; falls back to a plain status line in the quiet register or under reduced motion. Ported from the sketchbook's Kantar plate (a tiatr stage), principle rather than likeness (HOMAGE rule 1): the three-phase timeline and the curtain's own geometry (canvas-drawn from pure, tested functions), not the painted sets or the pit band. Makes no sound of its own (decision 0015); the song lines are placeholders awaiting a Konkani ear (HOMAGE rule 7).

budget.reason: Counted raw (comments included) since the registry measures source bytes: kantar.js (the DOM and timing driver, the spot, the singer) 13.6 KB and kantar.core.js (the pure timeline and the pure geometry, all tested) 10.7 KB, about 24.6 KB. The velvet, folds, shadow and fringe moved out to the shared kantar-curtain package, which the Kantar scene draws from too.

items.name: kernels-booking
items.title: Kernels: booking
items.description: Pure booking kernels from the Casa Exemplo redesign: ISO day arithmetic with no timezone drift, a rate card that keeps its provisional flags, quotes with every night, GST on its own line and the deposit, and availability with same-day turnover. No dependencies; runs in Node.

budget.reason: The five kernel files are 14,595 bytes; drift.test.js (2,389 bytes) ships with them so a consumer with its own copy can check it for drift, and it never loads in a page.

items.name: link
items.title: Link
items.description: A native <a href>, unchanged, with the register's underline drawn beneath it: quiet is a plain hairline underline; warm draws an ink line in on hover or focus and back out on leave; playful is the underline as a kolam line, one continuous wave with a small knotted loop. Forced colours bring back the browser's own underline.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today about 6.1 KB: behaviour (link.js + link.core.js) 3.4 KB, skins quiet 0.2 KB, warm 1.3 KB, playful 1.1 KB.

items.name: loader
items.title: Loader
items.description: A polite status region that says in words what is loading, with a small drawing beside it: three pulsing dots in quiet, a light travelling round a kolam and lighting each dot in warm, a spinning bambaram in playful. It never claims how far along the work is.

budget.reason: The contract's 12 KB behaviour plus 8 KB per skin, declared as the sum used: behaviour (loader.js) about 3.2 KB, including the status line that announces a newly added loader once; skins about 0.9 KB (quiet), 2.9 KB (warm) and 3.3 KB (playful). The warm skin reuses the Kolam scene's geometry.

items.name: menu
items.title: Menu
items.description: A menu and price list a small food business can run on a phone. The page's own semantic list (sections of dishes, each with a name, price in rupees, unit, sauce line, tags as words and an available, sold-out or ask-first status) reads fine with no script; with it, `orderable` adds a quantity stepper per dish (native buttons, one polite live total) and an sg-change event with the lines and the total. Quiet is a typeset price list with leader dots and tabular figures; warm a menu card with a hand-ruled double frame and script section heads; playful price pills and chips where the count settles once when a dish is added.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 26533 bytes with comments (19083 as code): element, pure core and three skins (warm 3 KB for the ruled frame, playful 1 KB).

items.name: narration
items.title: Narration
items.description: Recorded or synthesised speech plus a WebVTT timing track that drives captions and word-by-word highlighting. A pure timing core (phrase splitting, a WAV duration reader, script-aware word weights with a real Devanagari and Kannada akshara segmenter, a WebVTT writer and parser), a provider interface with a Sarvam bulbul adapter and an offline silent-WAV stub, a fixture cache keyed on the request so tests and demos never call the network, the <sg-narration> highlight driver, and an offline speechSynthesis fallback.

budget.reason: A package budget in the shape of engine and tokens (decision 0001), not a component's 12/8 KB split: the pure timing core, three providers, the fixture cache and the DOM highlight driver together, today 40355 bytes, with headroom for the Sarvam adapter to grow as the API does.

items.name: now-note
items.title: Now note
items.description: A short, dated note of what someone is up to right now, with the availability as a badge in words. It adds how long ago it was updated and, past a stale-after limit, says plainly that it may be out of date. Quiet is a dated line; warm is a sticky note in the hand; playful is a café chalkboard in a wooden frame.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 5921 bytes: element 3.0 KB, pure core 2.2 KB, skins quiet 0.1 KB, warm 0.4 KB, playful 0.2 KB. The state is the badge component.

items.name: otp
items.title: One-time code
items.description: A one-time code entry. The native path is one input with autocomplete="one-time-code" and the number pad, which submits, takes SMS autofill and works without JavaScript. With JavaScript the same input lies transparently over a row of aria-hidden boxes: typing over a box replaces it, backspace works back across them, and a paste keeps just the digits. Quiet is plain boxes; warm stamp boxes that ink each digit; playful a stamp per digit.

budget.reason: Decision 0009: behaviour declared at 14 KB (the box-by-box editing model over one native input, and digits from every Indian script and full width read as ASCII), plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today: behaviour 13.0 KB (otp.js 7.5, otp.core.js 5.6); skins share 1.6 KB of boxes, quiet adds 0.2 KB, warm 2.4 KB, playful 0.4 KB plus warm.

items.name: player
items.title: Player
items.description: The Susegad player: enhances a native video or audio element with a drawn scrubber, captions in our type, a poster that is a scene's still, WebGL video treatments (ink, halftone, duotone, riso) and timed ink annotations on the moving frame. Content sound plays only on its own play press.

budget.reason: Wider than a typical component's 12-16 KB (0009) because it carries four sub-systems a normal component doesn't: a WebGL video-treatment renderer (treatments.js, 8.3 KB after gating the black-canvas-before-first-frame fix behind a ready callback, plus its tested colour/halftone core), a poster renderer that drives a whole scene once (poster.js, 1.9 KB), an ink-annotation overlay (annotations.js, 2.7 KB) and the bar/captions/keyboard behaviour itself (player.js, 15.7 KB after the frame-wrapper, focusability and stroke-icon fixes, over the 12 KB default; declared here rather than split further, since the parts already separate cleanly into their own files and cores). Skins grew to 2.4 KB each (still well inside 8 KB) once they positioned the scrubber canvas against the range's own box, rather than the whole bar, per Sutradhar's review. Pure cores (player.core.js 3.0 KB, annotations.core.js 3.7 KB, treatments.core.js 3.7 KB = 10.4 KB) stay inside the 12 KB core allowance (0010) even summed. Measured total 44.5 KB; budgeted with a little headroom. This is closer to a scene's budget than a component's; worth a decision addendum if more AV components follow this shape.

items.name: popover
items.title: Popover
items.description: A trigger and a native [popover], unchanged: popovertarget opens, closes, focuses and light-dismisses it with or without JavaScript. Quiet is a hairline card; warm is an inland-letter card with a folded corner; playful adds a dashed postmark. Placement uses CSS anchor positioning where supported, and a pure, tested fallback elsewhere.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today about 5.5 KB: behaviour (popover.js + popover.core.js) 4.7 KB; skins quiet, warm and playful are each a no-op mount (about 0.2 KB each), because the look is entirely in popover.css keyed off [data-skin].

items.name: postcard
items.title: Postcard
items.description: A card for a piece of work: title, where and when with a status badge beside them, the problem in a line, what was built and the outcome. The heading's link is stretched over the card, so each card is one tab stop with nothing nested. A rubber stamp for the status is opt-in (status-style="stamp"). Quiet is an index card; warm is the back of a picture postcard on deckled card stock with a printed postage square (a postmark on the stamp when there is one); playful is set down crooked and turns over on hover or focus, and lies flat on touch screens and under reduced motion.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 9427 bytes: element 2.8 KB, pure core 2.4 KB, skins quiet 0.2 KB, warm 3.1 KB, playful 1.1 KB. The status is the badge component by default; the stamp is opt-in and the builder adds it.

items.name: pretext
items.title: Pretext (vendored)
items.description: Cheng Lou's Pretext, an ESM build of main at e73081f (MIT): multiline text measured and laid out by arithmetic over cached widths, with each browser's own line breaker. Used only through the type tier, and loaded only when a scene sets words in the world. Its bytes are recorded apart from ours (decision 0019).

budget.reason: Vendored and never edited: the exact bytes of the pinned build, so any change to it fails the build until it is recorded (decision 0019).

items.name: progress
items.title: Progress
items.description: Enhances a native progress element. Quiet is the native bar as a pencil hairline; warm is a small kolam drawn exactly as far as the value, closing at 100%; playful is a cutting-chai glass that fills with tea. It moves only when the value moves, and without a value it says in words what is happening.

budget.reason: The contract's 12 KB behaviour plus 8 KB per skin, declared as the sum used: behaviour (progress.js) about 4.4 KB, skins about 0.2 KB (quiet), 3.6 KB (warm) and 6.3 KB (playful, including the slosh that never shows more than the value). The warm skin reuses the Kolam scene's geometry rather than carrying its own.

items.name: proposal
items.title: Proposal
items.description: A proposal written in Markdown and built into one sealed Folio file: a cover with the Paus scene, who it is for and from, its date and how long it holds, and a stamped status while it is a draft; one section per heading; a rate card and stay prices worked out by the booking kernels, with other dates to try; a plan you can walk through with a native range; scope and cost tables that stack into labelled cards on a phone; terms; and a signing block with the options as native radios and <sg-signature>. It reads, prints and can be signed on paper without JavaScript. The page builder (proposal.page.js, build.mjs) runs in Node beside Folio and is not copied.

items.name: quote
items.title: Quote
items.description: A pull-quote or testimonial in a native figure: the words, who said them, their role and business, and an optional link to the source. Quiet sets the words beside a hairline with the name in small capitals; warm writes them in the hand as a margin note with a pencil bracket; playful sets them large under a hand-drawn quotation mark that inks in once.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 7520 bytes: element 1.4 KB, pure core 3.1 KB, skins quiet 0.2 KB, warm 1.5 KB, playful 1.3 KB.

items.name: radio
items.title: Radio group
items.description: A real fieldset of native radios: arrow keys, one choice per name, required and submitting all stay the browser's, with or without JavaScript. Quiet is hairline circles drawn by CSS; warm draws pencil circles and circles the choice in ink, a leaning oval that runs past its start; playful turns the choice into a four-petalled kolam flower. Forced colours bring back the system radios.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 10824 bytes: behaviour (radio.js + radio.core.js) 6.2 KB, skins quiet 0.2 KB, warm 2.7 KB, playful 1.5 KB.

items.name: reach
items.title: Reach
items.description: A contact block in an address: email and WhatsApp as real links (built by waLink and mailtoLink), a copy-the-number button that appears only where the clipboard works and says in words that it copied, and a line on reply times. Quiet is plain lines; warm is an inland letter that stays pale blue at night; playful is a rubber-stamped card with the stamp's own ink starvation on its frame.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 8457 bytes: element 3.8 KB, pure core 2.1 KB, skins quiet 0.1 KB, warm 0.2 KB, playful 2.3 KB (the ink mask is the stamp's, reused).

items.name: room-details
items.title: Room details
items.description: A guest-facing room card for a homestay. A skeleton stands in until the room's details really arrive, then inks them in: a painted view, name, beds, the rate in rupees with Indian digit grouping, what is included, and availability as a badge. If the details cannot be loaded it says so plainly, with Try again. Driven by a pure, seeded fake source you swap for your own.

items.name: saving-footer
items.title: Saving footer
items.description: A form that saves itself when the person pauses typing, with a footer that says Saving, Saved at 14:32, or why it could not save. Offline, it shows the connection with fireflies and saves by itself once the connection is back. Driven by a pure, seeded fake transport you swap for your own.

items.name: scene-abri
items.title: Abri
items.description: Deccani cloud paper being made: drops of indigo, ochre, madder and grey-green land on a tray of size and push each other into rings by the area-preserving marbling map, a stylus combs them, a curl drift billows them, and a sheet is laid, lifted and turned to show its print. Quiet is the print as a still; warm makes sheet after sheet; playful takes a hand in the size (pointer, or arrow keys and Enter to drop a colour).

items.name: scene-chai
items.title: Chai
items.description: Three small ink drawings on one sheet, meant as a loader, a toggle and a divider: a cutting-chai glass whose steam follows a curl-noise field, a clay diya whose flame leans from the pointer and goes out with a curl of smoke, and a tulsi creeper that grows along a rule. Set lit to put the lamp out or light it. Quiet is the plate's still; warm steams and flickers; playful takes a tap on the flame and a hover on the creeper.

items.name: scene-chiro
items.title: Chiro
items.description: A Goan laterite compound wall up close through a year: the pits in each cut block grow as a Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion, the monsoon darkens the stone from the top, moss creeps out of the joints and the sun bleaches it back. Quiet is the monsoon-green still; warm an easier year; playful takes a hand (pointer, or arrow keys and Enter) that leaves a damp print, and a brush that rubs red dust loose.

budget.reason: The plate's simulation, colouring pass and pencil work, ported line for line.

items.name: scene-dar
items.title: Dar
items.description: Yours to keep: a Goan house front in elevation, with a laterite wall under lime plaster, a painted door in a lime-white surround, a window of oyster-shell panes and bougainvillea. A key on a ring with a wooden tag swings in, catches on the brass hook by the door and sways to rest, and the tower bolt slides home. Quiet is a hairline elevation; playful swings the key and slides the bolt.

items.name: scene-ferry
items.title: Ferry
items.description: Four stops across the Mandovi: a river ferry in ballpoint hatching, with a small jetty on the far side, two channel posts and a big jetty on the near bank, each with a lamp. The step attribute sails it to a stop; absent, it idles at the first and never moves on by itself. Quiet is a hairline still; playful advances a stop on a click and a kite circles.

budget.reason: a whole river view drawn by hand: far bank, jetties, posts, near bank, a canoe and the ferry, in ink and in hairline

items.name: scene-ghat
items.title: Ghat
items.description: A survey sheet of the Western Ghats above Goa: contours traced out of a noise height field with marching squares, rivers that find their own way to the sea, a ghat road that switchbacks up the escarpment, hand lettering, and monsoon clouds catching on the ridge. progress inks it from sea level up (a page can tie it to its own scroll); the pointer, or the keyboard hand in playful, reads the height of the ground as text.

budget.reason: The plate's terrain, drainage, contour, road and lettering code, ported line for line.

items.name: scene-kairi
items.title: Kairi
items.description: A printed sari border drawn by a machine of spinning circles: each paisley's outline is a Fourier series, the chain grows one circle at a time until the pencil sketch sharpens, then the pen inks it and madder, indigo and turmeric fill it. Set progress from real work and the border is drawn exactly that far ("40% done"). Quiet is the finished border, warm draws it once and rests, playful draws border after border and slows near the pointer; Enter goes on to the next paisley.

items.name: scene-kantar
items.title: Kantar
items.description: The tiatr stage and curtain: painted proscenium with gold-fringed pelmet, footlights, orchestra pit, and three backdrops (church square, dusk beach, balcão night) behind a heavy red velvet curtain. Quiet is a lit still; warm rises once and rests; playful cycles through scenes, curtain drops, and kantars sung in the spotlight.

budget.reason: The singer performs, the house sits in the front row and answers her, the pit plays in the same beat, and the painted flats carry form and shadows. Under the 64 KB ceiling in decision 0003.

items.name: scene-khazan
items.title: Khazan
items.description: Fireflies over a Goan tidal wetland at night: some four hundred phase oscillators with Kuramoto coupling fall into step in slow waves, with additive glows and rippling reflections. Quiet is a still of a wave passing through the bank; warm lets them find each other; playful lets a hand scatter them. Set progress and the bank is exactly that far in step: a calm loader for syncs and uploads.

items.name: scene-kolam
items.title: Kolam
items.description: One unbroken line of rice flour around a grid of dots, found with the mirror-curve method. Hairline ink in quiet, drawn once at a hand's pace in warm, poured by your hand with rangoli colour and ants in playful. The progress attribute draws it exactly that far.

items.name: scene-mankurad
items.title: Mankurad
items.description: A short story about a mango in coloured pencil: it ripens in the May heat while a koel calls, clouds come in, the first monsoon rain falls, and it drops into a puddle on red laterite. Hatched tone, boiling outlines, a noise-driven pendulum. Quiet is the plate's still; warm tells the story at an easy pace; playful tells it again on Enter. Set progress and the story holds at that beat, a gentle order or delivery tracker.

budget.reason: The plate's painters and sprite cache for a whole short story, ported line for line.

items.name: scene-maun
items.title: Maun
items.description: A colour field that paints itself in thin veils, rolled on and scraped back so a warm ground glows through, then rests with only a slow breath of light. Four palettes (turmeric, monsoon, kokum, indigo on lime); the same seed is always the same painting. A quiet background for words and a document cover; in playful, a click scrapes a band back. After V. S. Gaitonde's method, not his pictures.

items.name: scene-mithagar
items.title: Mithagar
items.description: The Ribandar salt pans at dawn: a geometric grid of clay bunds, shallow brine reflecting the Goan sky, wooden sluice gates, crystalline white salt crusts, and pyramidal salt heaps. Evaporation recedes the brine and grows the harvest. Quiet is a crisp architectural grid; warm ripples the water; playful lets sandpipers scurry and clicks rake salt pyramids.

budget.reason: The field reflects one continuous sky sampled per pan, the salt takes the ground as a moving front, a raker works the near pan, and the sky and bunds are cached so the scene runs at the baseline. Under the 64 KB ceiling in decision 0003.

items.name: scene-mosaico
items.title: Mosaico
items.description: The cement-tile floor of an old Goan balcão, seen from above: one Truchet tile laid in two turns, so the oxide-red bands join into long winding ribbons, worn and chipped under late window light. Now and then a tile lifts and turns and the ribbons re-route, and a small ant walks the pale line down one ribbon, following the new way. In playful, hover or Enter turns a tile and a click re-lays a patch. Dark pages get the same floor at night.

items.name: scene-neel
items.title: Neel
items.description: Hand block printing on khadi cotton: a carved buti block generated from the seed is pressed one impression at a time, indigo outlines first, then a second colour off register, every impression a little starved and turned. Quiet is the finished length; warm prints it at an unhurried pace and rests; playful prints faster and presses where you click or press Enter. Set progress and exactly that share is printed: a loader that shows real work.

items.name: scene-nod
items.title: Nod
items.description: The helper that asks first: a cutting chai steams beside a phone on a marble café table; a message arrives, a helper drafts a reply in a dashed card with an empty tick, and it goes out only when a person nods. Warm plays one exchange with a finger's tap; playful waits for your click or Enter; quiet is the draft, waiting.

items.name: scene-pahat
items.title: Pahat
items.description: The desk at dawn: a barred window at half past four over a laptop and a steel tumbler. The sky goes from indigo to first light, the stars fade, the morning star holds on, the room comes out of the dark and a few birds cross; then it rests. Quiet is a hairline still; in playful your hand moves the dawn.

items.name: scene-paus
items.title: Paus
items.description: The monsoon through a Goan window: rain beads, merges and runs down fogged glass. Hosts text in calm zones, clears from the sill up with progress, and wipes under a finger or the arrow keys.

budget.reason: The heavy baseline scene: drop simulation, fog mask, dusk palette, three registers.

items.name: scene-posta
items.title: Posta
items.description: The Old Post Office in Fontainhas: a vintage rosewood sorting desk beneath an oyster shell carepa window with sunbeams, wooden cubbies holding jute-tied letter bundles, a crimson postbox with brass flap, and a brass balance scale.

budget.reason: The room now carries a customer at the window and a beam that swings and narrows with the day, and the three contact sounds are shaped per voice instead of being one beep. Under the 64 KB ceiling in decision 0003.

items.name: scene-prahar
items.title: Prahar
items.description: A day over a Goan river village in the eight watches of raga time: the sky blended in OKLab, every land layer tinted to the light, the sun and moon on their arcs, lamps after dusk, and a ruler of the eight prahars with each raga in English and Devanagari. Set hour from the page's own clock for a theme that follows the viewer's day; in playful, drag the ruler. The raga-to-hour mapping is one common reckoning; traditions differ.

items.name: scene-rampon
items.title: Rampon
items.description: Dusk on the Goan shore: a ballpoint sea of short hatching strokes that boils like hand-drawn animation, a sun sinking into haze, palms swaying in seeded wind, a ramponkar's canoe with its net heaped inside, and a few distant birds. Quiet is a single still; warm boils gently; playful boils in full, a click draws a new evening, and a koel calls.

items.name: scene-saanj
items.title: Saanj
items.description: Dusk over flooded paddy: a sky mixed in OKLCH from apricot through rose to indigo, a line of ink palms, and a murmuration of six hundred rosy starlings flown by boids, which pours into the palms to roost and leaves at dawn. Quiet is one finished frame of the murmuration; warm an easier dusk with a smaller flock; playful makes the pointer, or the arrow keys, a hawk the flock parts around. The flock flies round slotted text.

budget.reason: The plate's own OKLCH colour, boids flock, paddy plots and palms, ported line for line.

items.name: scene-shet
items.title: Shet
items.description: One year of a Goan paddy field seen from a low rise: cracked April mud, the first rain darkening it drop by drop, flooded plots, green rice combed by wind, ripe gold, the harvest, and the mud cracking again, with two cattle egrets that come with the water. Quiet is the ripening gold as a finished still, warm turns the year at an easier pace, playful gives the wind to the hand. Set progress and the field holds at that point of the year. A scape: the still loads first, the turning year after.

budget.reason: A year in a field, the plate's own code: its still is under 64 KB of code (first sight), the whole year under 96 KB of source, comments kept.

items.name: scene-taverna
items.title: Taverna
items.description: Rain on bottle glass: a village taverna window on a rainy monsoon night with dark wooden bars, dark green wine bottles, a ceramic jug, and a slate blackboard. Outside, rain sweeps down a cobblestone alley under a glowing streetlamp; on the glass, warm indoor air condenses and raindrops trickle in delicate rivulets. Quiet is a crisp ink elevation; warm settles gracefully; playful chimes the bottles and wipes the misted glass.

budget.reason: Adds the person crossing the alley under a lantern, the bar shadows it throws across the sill, and a struck-glass chime instead of a single tone. Under the 64 KB ceiling in decision 0003.

items.name: scene-themb
items.title: Themb
items.description: Rain on a taro leaf seen from above: a WebGL shader draws the velvet leaf, its inked veins and the beads as signed distance fields joined by a smooth minimum, each a lens over the leaf; a full 2D painting takes over when WebGL is missing, lost or too slow. Beads roll, merge keeping their area, gather in the cup, and the leaf pours them off its tip. Quiet is the still after a shower; warm an easier rain; playful tilts under the pointer or arrow keys, and Enter pours.

budget.reason: Two complete renderers: the WebGL shader and a full 2D fallback, with the plate's physics.

items.name: scene-tinto
items.title: Tinto
items.description: A crowded Goan village square at half past ten, where every figure has a line: the poder on his round, a fish seller and her cat, a card game under the tree, the bus to Mapusa. Point at anyone to read their line; every line is also real text for screen readers. Quiet is a still, warm an easy morning with a slow round of captions, playful the full square with a keyboard hand. For empty states and 404s (focus pins one line). With words="world", the page’s words are chalked on a board outside the Taverna and each shop hangs its hours on a plaque that opens its detail; quiet and small screens keep them flat.

budget.reason: Seventeen vignettes ported line for line from the plate, and words in the world: the chalkboard, the plaques and the lazy type tier (the tier and Pretext are counted apart).

items.name: scene-tollem
items.title: Tollem
items.description: Looking down into a Goan pool at noon: a WebGL net of light over pale tiles, a frangipani that drops a flower now and then, and a full 2D painting when WebGL is missing, lost or too slow. Quiets under text, shows progress as a flower's place across the pool, and ripples under a finger or the arrow keys.

budget.reason: Two complete renderers: the WebGL shader and a full 2D fallback.

items.name: scene-toran
items.title: Toran
items.description: A Goan doorway on the morning of Chovoth, with a garland of marigolds and mango leaves strung across it from three nails: a Verlet rope that sags, swings in a noise breeze and settles. Quiet is the garland at rest with petals on the step; warm a gentle breeze; playful the full breeze, and the hand (pointer or arrow keys) brushes it, knocking petals loose that drift down and stay. Night with a lantern on dark pages.

budget.reason: The plate's whole doorway (wall, frame, teak door, step, balcão, eave, lota, chappals) and its marigold sprites are painted in code, ported line for line.

items.name: scene-vad
items.title: Vad
items.description: A banyan grows in pen and ink by space colonisation: branch tips reach for the nearest points of an umbrella canopy, limbs thicken by the pipe model, leaf masses are hatched over a green wash, and aerial roots drop and thicken into pillar trunks round a stone platform. Quiet is the grown tree; warm grows it slowly and lets the ink boil; playful grows a new one on Enter. Set progress and the tree grows exactly as far as the work has. With words="world", the page’s words are written in the sky beside the tree, each line ending where the canopy begins, and make room for it four times as it grows.

items.name: scene-vahi
items.title: Vahi
items.description: The pile becomes a ledger: loose receipts, invoices, a bill book and a scrawled chit lift one at a time from a teak table, drift over an open account book while their line is written, and settle on a neat stack; then the book closes and its string is wound. Quiet is a hairline plan of the closed book and the stack; playful scatters the pile at a click. The progress attribute sorts exactly that much.

budget.reason: four kinds of paper, the book that closes, a pen, a clip and a string, each painted by hand in ink and in hairline

items.name: scene-vel
items.title: Vel
items.description: A magenta bougainvillea grows from behind a laterite compound wall by a seeded L-system, arches up and spills down the lime-washed cap, drawn as inline SVG. Quiet is the grown vine as a still, warm grows it and lets a breeze move a few tips while a bract lets go now and then, playful stirs the branch under the hand and shakes bracts loose. For heroes and seasonal sections over a wall of text.

budget.reason: Two worlds ported line for line from the plate: the L-system vine with its turtle, taper and growth schedule, and the laterite wall with its sky, palms, pits, stains, cap and ground; the SVG renderer then drives every animation from the scene clock.

items.name: scene-veranda
items.title: Veranda
items.description: A Goan veranda drawn in ink and wash, seen from a seat on it: laterite pillars with a balcão between them, a teak door and a shuttered window in a lime-washed wall, a brass lamp under the rafters, and the garden and paddy beyond. The pillars' shadows are traced from the same solids as the drawing, and so is an exact depth map (white near, sky 0) that lets <sg-depth-photo treatment="drawn"> rack focus and walk the camera in. Quiet is a hairline still, warm sways the lamp, playful lets your hand move the sun, and the dark theme is dusk with the lamp lit. A scape: the still loads first.

budget.reason: A ray-cast drawing, 70 KB of source with its comments: the world and its ray caster 15.8 KB, the painter 35.0 KB, the renderer 6.5 KB, the model 2.7 KB, meta 6.3 KB. First sight is the still, 55.7 KB of code (under 64 KB); assets.js (2.9 KB), which writes the depth and layers maps for the 3D stage, loads only on a page that stages it.

items.name: scroll-section
items.title: Scroll section
items.description: A section whose content -- most often a child <sg-scene>'s progress -- advances as it travels through the viewport, following the Ghat plate's scroll arithmetic. An IntersectionObserver plus a scroll-event safety net (for a fast jump that could skip the observer's near zone) drive the numeric progress a scene needs, since only JavaScript can set an attribute; a genuinely CSS-only reveal layer (.sg-scroll-reveal) uses native animation-timeline: view() where the browser has it, with no JavaScript at all. Quiet and reduced motion never scrub: the section hands its scene straight back to the scene's own still.

budget.reason: Decision 0005/0010: 12 KB behaviour (scroll-section.js + scroll-section.core.js) plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 9679 bytes: behaviour 8.5 KB, skins quiet 0.3 KB, warm 0.5 KB, playful 0.3 KB.

items.name: select
items.title: Select
items.description: The browser's own select, kept native: its keyboard, its screen-reader role and its place in the form are untouched. Where customizable select is supported, CSS draws the button, the caret and the picker: a hairline box and list in quiet; in warm the select is written on the paper, over the field's pencil rule, with a caret of two pencil strokes and ink over the rule under a chosen value; in playful a stamped box with an accent caret, and stamped chips.

budget.reason: Behaviour (select.js) about 2.3 KB; skins about 0.2 KB (quiet), 1.6 KB (warm) and 0.6 KB (playful). Most of the look is CSS on the native element. The warm skin draws with field/rule.js (about 3.1 KB, counted in field).

items.name: signature
items.title: Signature
items.description: Sign by hand or by typing your name. The native path is a typed-name input that submits and works without JavaScript; with it, a pad takes a finger, pen or mouse, inks the stroke from the pen's pressure and speed, and submits the ink as SVG path data in a hidden input. Undo and start again are real buttons. Quiet is a plain line and a plain pen; warm a broad nib whose fresh ink dries into the paper; playful adds a flourish.

budget.reason: Decision 0009: behaviour declared at 15 KB (the ink ribbon lives in the element, because the submitted path must be exactly the ink shown), plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today: behaviour 14.3 KB (signature.js 8.6, signature.core.js 5.7); the skins share a 9.6 KB painter (skins/paint.js 7.2 and skins/marks.js 2.4: baking, drying, grain, the typed name, the flourish), and each skin file is under 0.4 KB. A page loads one skin and the painter, 10.0 KB, which is over the 8 KB per skin; the painter is one piece of work, split no further.

items.name: site-nav
items.title: Site nav
items.description: A site header that works with no JavaScript: the page links sit in a native details, a Menu button on narrow screens and a row on wide ones, with the current page in aria-current. No dialog or drawer. Quiet is plain links over a hairline rule; warm writes them in the hand with a pencil line under the current page; playful makes them stamped tabs.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 8623 bytes: element 3.7 KB, pure core 2.5 KB, skins quiet 0.2 KB, warm 1.6 KB, playful 0.6 KB.

items.name: site-shell
items.title: Site shell
items.description: Proves Wave 5's pieces work together on one page for a fictional homestay, Casa Aldona: a header with Tabs (Overview, Rooms, Book) and a Menu (Account), a Dialog ("Ask the house"), a Drawer (the rooms), a scroll section driving the Paus scene by real scroll, and a Kantar interlude between two steps of a small booking flow. Every piece is a plain library part; this recipe adds no new theatre of its own, only the composition and a tiny two-step flow state (site-shell.core.js). Without JavaScript every section shows and Dialog/Drawer's openers are real links to a real page.

items.name: skeleton
items.title: Skeleton
items.description: A placeholder for a region whose content is on its way. The region is aria-busy and says what is loading, then announces the arrival once. Quiet is flat sunk blocks; warm is a pencil sketch whose outlines ink in when the content arrives; playful adds colour washes and a wobble on twos while waiting.

budget.reason: The contract's 12 KB behaviour plus 8 KB per skin, declared as the sum used: behaviour about 7.0 KB (skeleton.js 2.5 KB, skeleton.core.js 4.6 KB); skins about 1.3 KB (quiet), 5.5 KB of shared drawing (skins/draw.js: the layer every skin uses, plus the pencil for warm and playful), 1.1 KB (warm) and 2.3 KB (playful). A page loads one skin and draw.js.

items.name: sound
items.title: Sound
items.description: The synthesised UI vocabulary (tick, confirm, complete, gentle error) with Web Audio, no audio files. One global switch, off by default and remembered per viewer, that never sounds before a user gesture even when remembered on. Paired haptics on the same rules. Soundscapes live in sound/scapes/ and are added separately by the scene that uses them.

items.name: sound-scape-paus-rain
items.title: Paus rain
items.description: Each visible raindrop on Paus's glass becomes an audible tick, seeded like the drawing itself. Voice-limited and pooled (never more than a handful of oscillators at once, however hard it is raining), panned by where each drop sits and pitched a little higher for a smaller one. Only runs with the sound switch on, and stops when the scene leaves the viewport or the tab is hidden. attachPausRain(sceneEl) wires it to a live <sg-scene name="paus">.

items.name: sound-scape-rampon-koel
items.title: Rampon koel
items.description: A rising three-note "ku-oo" call in a bout of three that speeds up, then quiet, then another bout, the way a real koel calls. Only in playful, only with the switch on, and only while a bird is actually visible on screen, read from the same birdX() the scene draws its birds from. attachRamponKoel(sceneEl) wires it to a live <sg-scene name="rampon">.

items.name: sound-switch
items.title: Sound switch
items.description: The one control that turns Susegad's sound switch on or off, site-wide, over a native checkbox with role=switch. Checking it is the user's own gesture, so switch.js can resume the audio context right there and play the switch's own confirmation. Without JavaScript the checkbox still works as a switch but has no effect, and a note says so. Quiet is the plain switch; warm draws a small speaker with a slash when off and two arcs when on; playful breathes those arcs gently while on.

items.name: stage3d
items.title: Stage3d: the three.js tier
items.description: The lazy three.js tier (decision 0017): loadThree() imports three only when a live 3D drawing is about to be seen, and resolves null if it cannot; webglAvailable(), liteDevice() and watchVisible() choose and pause the tier; the pure core chooses live, 2D or still, reprojects a photo with a depth map so a moving camera gives true parallax, and fits it to any frame. Needs the npm package three at exactly 0.186.1.

budget.reason: Decision 0017: the tier is budgeted apart from the dependency-free layers. Today 10.0 KB: stage3d.js 4.3 KB (lazy loader, WebGL and software-renderer detection, visibility), stage3d.core.js 5.8 KB (pure, tested in Node). three itself (npmDependencies) is recorded per story as bundled.

items.name: stamp
items.title: Stamp
items.description: A mark that something real has happened: held, received, paid. The words are text in a role="status" region, announced once when it lands. Quiet is a ruled rectangle; warm is a tilted block print with seeded ink starvation and an off-register ghost; playful presses down and the ink spreads.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 14455 bytes: behaviour (stamp.js + stamp.core.js) 9.4 KB, skins quiet 0.6 KB, warm 4.0 KB, playful 0.4 KB plus warm.

items.name: stepper
items.title: Stepper
items.description: A long form walked one step at a time. Without JavaScript every step is a visible fieldset with one submit. With it, Back and Next, focus on each step's legend, progress in words, and nothing typed ever lost. Quiet is numbered stations; warm is a walk on a survey map, the road found round the hills with A*; playful adds footprints.

budget.reason: Behaviour about 11.7 KB (stepper.js 6.0 KB, stepper.core.js 5.6 KB with the terrain, A* and footprints); skins 1.2 KB (quiet), 4.5 KB of map shared by warm and playful (skins/map.js), 0.3 KB each for warm and playful. Total 17,973 bytes; declared at 20,480 for about 12% headroom (review W2 P12, as Wave 1 P7 asked), within decision 0009.

items.name: storybook-spread
items.title: The first rain (storybook spread)
items.description: One bilingual (English and Marathi), narrated spread of a Goan children's storybook: text beside the paus scene, word-by-word highlighting, always-present captions, and rain intensity driven by which words are playing, not the clock. Works without JavaScript: the story text and native audio controls and captions are always there.

items.name: studio-home
items.title: Studio home (a mock)
items.description: A one-person studio's home page from the studio-site pieces: a site nav, a now note, postcards for the work, a client's quote beside the redacted conversation it came from with a voice note in it, and a contact block. All copy is placeholder and says so. Reads in full without JavaScript, in any register.

items.name: surface-carepa
items.title: Carepa
items.description: A surface (decision 0016: a drawn backdrop, a pure model, a renderer and a still like a scene, but with no slotted reading zone of its own): a Goan window glazed with oyster shell, filling its host edge to edge (cover-fit): the warm and playful backdrop for Dialog and Drawer. The room is painted opaque, so nothing behind the surface is legible through it; the pointer is the sun, and each shell catches pink, green and blue at its own angle. A finished reduced-motion still and a plain translucent CSS fallback.

budget.reason: model.js (pure) + render.js (the renderer, cover-fit mount, the dusk palette for dark theme, cached pane paths, the idle skip and a Paus-style quality governor) + meta.js + index.js: 28,803 bytes. Raised from 23,552 when the governor landed (8edd386); still under a scene's 40 KB default. Decision 0016.

items.name: tabs
items.title: Tabs
items.description: A row of headed sections, read one at a time. Without JavaScript it is a table of contents: every section shows and each link jumps to its heading. With JavaScript it is the ARIA APG tabs pattern, automatic activation, and the selected tab is marked by an ink underline that travels to it: a static hairline in quiet, an eased line in warm, the same line with a bead in playful. Panel swaps use a same-document View Transition where the browser has one, else an instant swap.

budget.reason: Decision 0005/0010: 12 KB behaviour (tabs.js + tabs.core.js) plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 11601 bytes: behaviour 9.2 KB (tabs.js imports the shared packages/transitions/page.js helper rather than repeating its View Transition guard), skins quiet 0.2 KB, warm 0.9 KB, playful 1.1 KB.

items.name: three-named
items.title: three.js, shaken (vendored)
items.description: three 0.186.1 (MIT) bundled with esbuild down to the names the stage3d tier and the veranda's pot use, for setThreeLoader(): 136 KB gzipped against 193 KB for the whole module. Never edited by hand; PROVENANCE.md records the exact command, the size and the sha256 (decision 0017).

budget.reason: Vendored and never edited: the exact bytes of the pinned build, recorded apart from our own code (decision 0017). Any change to it must be recorded in PROVENANCE.md.

items.name: tile-band
items.title: Tile band
items.description: A band of hand-painted tiles for a border or a section divider: Goan azulejo, the blue-and-white tiles of the Portuguese-era houses and churches, with a majolica sister in cobalt, lemon yellow and leaf green. Four geometric and floral motifs (a rosette, a quatrefoil, quarter-circle corners, a vine) laid from a seed, painted once on a canvas and kept, crisp at any pixel ratio, running along the page or down it. Quiet is a cobalt hairline, flat; warm is a hand-painted glaze with brush variation and crackle; playful turns a tile a quarter when you touch it, and settles.

motif.gloss: Azulejo: the painted tiles of Goa's Portuguese-era houses and churches; majolica is its Mediterranean cousin.

budget.reason: Decision 0005 and 0010: element 12 KB, pure core 12 KB apart, skins 8 KB each with a shared helper counting as one. Today about 25.5 KB: element 2.0 KB, pure core 11.0 KB (four motifs as path data, the seeded laying, crackle, the turn), the canvas manager 6.5 KB and the painter 5.2 KB, three one-line skins. It is a component, not a scene, because its box is the band (a length and a thickness the page chooses, horizontal or vertical) and it has no loop: it is painted once, and a rAF runs only for the half second of a turn.

items.name: toast
items.title: Toast
items.description: Short messages that never take focus. A region holds two live regions (polite, and alert for errors) and a pile of letters: the newest in front, the rest peeking above, fanning out when pointed at or focused. Timing follows WCAG 2.2.1: reading time, no timeout for errors or actions, pause on hover, focus and hidden tab. Quiet is a ruled note; warm an inland letter that unfolds; playful adds a postmark that lands.

budget.reason: Decisions 0007 and 0009: two elements (<sg-toast-region> and <sg-toast>) at 14 KB of behaviour each, 28 KB for the pair (WCAG 2.2.1 timing, two live regions, the pile, and room for the pile so focus is never hidden, 2.4.11), plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 32445 bytes: behaviour (toast.js + toast.core.js) 25.1 KB, skins quiet 0.9 KB, warm 2.1 KB, playful 3.6 KB.

items.name: toggle
items.title: Toggle
items.description: A native switch (a checkbox with role="switch") that submits and takes Space with or without JavaScript. Quiet is a plain track and thumb drawn by CSS; warm is the brass tower bolt from a Goan door, sliding into its keeper; playful is a clay diya that lights, its flame flickering only while lit and on screen. Forced colours bring back the system control.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 9352 bytes: behaviour (toggle.js + toggle.core.js) 5.3 KB, skins quiet 0.3 KB, warm 2.2 KB, playful 1.6 KB.

items.name: tokens
items.title: Tokens
items.description: Colour (OKLCH, light and dark, Susegad, Casa and Azulejo palettes), type for Latin, Devanagari and Kannada, space, motion, sound names and the register, as CSS custom properties with a JS mirror. Self-hosted OFL fonts split by script. Includes palette-from-photo.
items.stabilityReason: Colour, type, space, motion and the register cascade: every other piece is built on it, and it has carried real pages since the soft launch.

items.name: tooltip
items.title: Tooltip
items.description: A trigger and its accessible description, always linked by aria-describedby so the text reaches assistive technology whether or not it is shown. Quiet is a plain small label; warm hand-letters it; playful adds a pencil leader line. Without JavaScript, CSS alone reveals it by opacity on hover and focus. With JavaScript it becomes a popover (hint where understood, else manual), positioned above the trigger and flipped below when there is little room, by a pure, tested placement().

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today about 7.3 KB: behaviour (tooltip.js + tooltip.core.js) 6.6 KB; skins quiet, warm and playful are each a no-op mount (about 0.2 KB each), because the look is entirely in tooltip.css keyed off [data-skin]/[data-open]/[data-above].

items.name: transitions
items.title: Page transitions
items.description: Cross-document View Transitions for every same-origin navigation (@view-transition { navigation: auto; }), with two named persistent elements (data-vt="header" and data-vt="scene") that carry across a navigation instead of cross-fading, and sameDocumentTransition(), a tiny shared guard for a same-document swap (used by Tabs and the Kantar interlude). No JavaScript is required for the cross-document behaviour; without View Transitions support, or under reduced motion, navigation and same-document swaps are simply instant.

budget.reason: Not a component (no register, no skins): a CSS file plus a small pure helper. Today 3090 bytes of JS (page.js + page.core.js); page.css (1.7 KB) is not counted against the JS budget.

items.name: type
items.title: Type tier
items.description: Words set in the world, still real text: lay a heading and a paragraph into a drawn surface's real shape (a board, an arch, a slanted sign), one width per line; shrink-wrap and balance a card; fit the largest legible size or hand the words back to the flat reading; and place one DOM span per line, with the line boxes in the scene's logical units for calm and contrast. Loaded lazily; built on Pretext (decision 0019).

budget.reason: A pure layout core (layout.js) and its DOM edge (lines, junctions and surfaces), budgeted apart from Pretext's own bytes (decisions 0010 and 0019).

items.name: veranda-stage
items.title: Veranda stage
items.description: <sg-veranda-stage>: the drawn veranda staged in 3D through <sg-depth-photo>, with the page's words on a frosted pane inside it. The words stay real text; drag the grip (core's movable) to move the pane across the picture, PageUp and PageDown or the wheel to bring it forward or send it back, and things in front of it, read from the exact depth map, hide it. Focus follows the pane's depth, and the pane keeps itself readable and clear of every other set of words (the notes, the pot's pane) on release and whenever the camera, the lens or a note changes what is in front. Three.js loads only when the picture will move, from the smaller vendored build. In playful the pane becomes a lens on the veranda in the monsoon or at dusk. Notes stick to places (the door, the seat, the lamp), follow the camera and are found by the depth map under a drop; scrolling can walk the camera down the veranda, stopping at each note. A paragraph marked data-flow sits on its own glass pane at a clay pot that three.js turns on the balcao, the lines set round the pot's silhouette (a still on the 2D tier). Quiet and narrow screens keep the words flat.

budget.reason: 83 KB of source with comments across four files: the element 47 KB (the pane, its depth mask made for the camera as it stands, the settle that keeps the words clear of other words, the lens, the notes and the walk), matka-view.js 13 KB (three.js pot, its glass pane and the flowing paragraph, loaded only when a data-flow paragraph is present), and two pure cores, pane.core.js 18 KB and matka.core.js 4 KB, tested in Node and budgeted apart per decision 0010. It was 65,536 before the fix round that made the words never sit over other words and never hide while the camera moves (+17 KB, 11 KB of it the pure core, which the comments explain at length because three of the bugs it prevents were found only by looking at pixels); raised by the worker so the build passes, and flagged: the element is well over what a component usually declares, and the lens, notes and walk could move into a lazily loaded file, which is for the Sutradhar to decide. three.js is recorded apart (decision 0017): 135,588 B gzipped in the vendored build.

items.name: voice-note
items.title: Voice note
items.description: A voice message the way a phone shows it: a play button, a waveform you can seek along, the length, and the transcript always on show. It enhances a native audio element and plays only when its own button is pressed. The waveform comes from real loudness measured at build time, or is a seeded stand-in marked as one. Quiet is a hairline row with square bars; warm has pencil bars and an inked ring; playful is a bright pill whose button springs.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today about 17.3 KB: element 5.9 KB, pure core 4.6 KB, the build-time peaks tool 2.7 KB, skins share bars.js 2.5 KB (one shared helper counts as one skin, decision 0010) with quiet 0.2 KB, warm 0.3 KB, playful 0.8 KB. The time maths, cue lookup, VTT parser and WAV reader are reused from player and narration, not copied.

items.name: wa-order
items.title: WhatsApp order
items.description: The order composer for a small food business: it turns a menu selection into a pre-written WhatsApp message. It asks for the day (respecting a notice in hours), a time of day, delivery or pickup, the area, a name and any notes, shows the exact message ("This is what we'll send") and keeps the Send link's wa.me address equal to it. The plain wa.me link stays in the markup, so with no script it still opens WhatsApp. It never says an order is placed: the person sends the message themselves. Quiet is ruled fields, a plain bordered message and one ink-filled button; warm sets the message on ruled paper in the hand; playful is a speech bubble and a button that presses.

budget.reason: Decision 0005: 12 KB of behaviour plus 8 KB for each of three skins. Today 29534 bytes with comments (22252 as code): element 11 KB, pure core 15 KB (numbers, dates, the message, shortening), skins small.
